title: Masked readers distinguish the v101 terminal curls in three jointly resolved pairs
statement: Two independently prompted readers each saw ten whole-word crops from five new same-stem pairs and four older controls. On the seven new crops both readers could resolve, both assigned the same class and agreed with the v101 reading. Counting unresolved as missing matches gives nine of ten and seven of ten for the two readers. Both saw fewer short strokes before N than n in the three jointly resolved pairs. The first reader resolved the same direction in one additional pair; f80r remained unresolved in the within-pair test. Three of four controls matched each reader’s expected class. One attempted new pair was rejected before annotation because adjacent-line ink obscured the terminal. These are image-model judgments on selected matched words, so the reading difference supports a graphic contrast in this sample and can motivate human annotation.
check: Have human readers replicate the masked count on both sets with fixed criteria for separating the terminal return curl from the preceding letter. Preserve unresolved crops, test controls separately, and report exact agreement, broad curl-family agreement and pair-relative comparisons. Use a stratified selection of further folios to test whether the effect survives the original study’s same-page and nearest-match selection.

plan.scope: New manuscript folios from the public practice training partition; exclude every physical folio in pilot #511. Test visual terminal curls classified by two independent blinded model readers using the same neutral reference shapes as the pilot.
plan.selection: Use the case-sensitive pinned v101 reading. Restrict to certain paragraph words of length at least three ending in n or N with identical preceding strings on the same page. Take one pair per physical folio and at most three folios per hand for hands 1, 2, 3. Rank by absolute line-number distance, then absolute within-line ordinal difference, canonical page order, uppercase line and ordinal, and lowercase line and ordinal. Inspect the first three per hand or all where fewer than three exist. Keep failures to match the scan visible. Read only complete pairs in the primary comparison.
plan.controls: Mix in the same four calibrated control crops from #511 using their native scan pixels, including two longer curls and two other endings. They are excluded from the denominator for the new sample.
plan.blinding: Separate crop preparers from readers. Generate random opaque IDs and independent display order per reader. Send only a numbered image panel, a keyhole chart relabelled A, B, C, and the fixed classification rubric. Readers have no page IDs, word strings, pair assignments, or access to one another's response.
plan.outcomes: A = terminal return curl with zero independent short strokes preceding it; B = exactly one; C = two or more; D = visually different terminal; U = unresolved. Report all attempted and accepted pairs, joint readable denominator, broad curl-family versus other agreement, exact agreement, agreement with v101 (N maps to A, n maps to B), undecided rates, and whether relative stroke count is smaller, tied, larger, or unresolved for N versus n in the matching pair. Report by hand descriptively. Leave human rereading and inference about separate letters outside the measured claim.

reject.reason: A long stroke from the preceding line meets or crosses the second word’s terminal extension.

pilot_replay: The registered classifier agreement table and nearest-pair results reproduce exactly using the published score script. No new judgments were assigned to the prior targets. The four control crops are included in the new panel.

quality.preparation: Three preparers used adjacent word sequences to locate complete words independently of the readers. Individual source regions list the neighboring ink where relevant. No neighboring mark was digitally erased.

quality.limits: Five pairs were selected for a shared v101 stem, nearby text and an identifiable complete word. The result does not estimate all terminal-locus frequencies or identify the marks as separate letters. The two readers were fresh isolated image agents without access to the folio identities, word strings, expected categories, pairing, or each other’s judgments.

scripts.panels.py:
"""Make two randomly ordered masked panels using unchanged Yale crop pixels."""
import json
from pathlib import Path
from random import Random
import sys

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont

work = Path(sys.argv[1])
old = work.parent / 'voynich-v101-scan-work'
source = Path('experiments/K-010-open-1/mubadala777/step.json')
new = json.loads((work / 'selected-crops.json').read_text())
old_rows = json.loads(source.read_text())['results']['trials']
controls = [row for row in old_rows if row['v101_shape'] in ('C','D')]
rows = [{'locus': row['locus'], 'word_ordinal': row['word_ordinal'], 'v101': row['v101'],
         'xyxy': row['xyxy'], 'scan_crop': row['scan_crop'], 'source': 'control', 'expected': row['v101_shape']}
        for row in controls]
rows += [dict(row, source='new', expected={'N':'A','n':'B'}[row['v101'][-1]]) for row in new]
rows.sort(key=lambda row:(row['locus'],row['word_ordinal']))
rng = Random(374201)
labels = rng.sample(range(100, 1000), len(rows))
for label, row in zip(labels, rows):
    row['tile'] = f'Q{label:03d}'
(work / 'sealed-key.json').write_text(json.dumps(rows, indent=2) + '\n')

font = ImageFont.truetype('/usr/share/fonts/truetype/dejavu/DejaVuSans.ttf', 18)
columns, width, height = 3, 320, 140
for reader, seed in [('a',49741),('b',92651)]:
    shuffled = list(rows)
    Random(seed).shuffle(shuffled)
    panel = Image.new('RGB', (columns * width, ((len(rows)+columns-1)//columns)*height), 'white')
    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(panel)
    for i,row in enumerate(shuffled):
        page = row['locus'].partition('.')[0]
        image_path = (old if row['source']=='control' else work) / f'{page}.jpg'
        with Image.open(image_path) as image:
            letter = image.crop(tuple(row['xyxy']))
        scale = min(1.5, 290 / letter.width, 104 / letter.height)
        letter = letter.resize((round(letter.width * scale),round(letter.height * scale)), Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
        x,y = (i % columns)*width,(i // columns)*height
        draw.text((x+8,y+3),row['tile'],font=font,fill='black')
        panel.paste(letter,(x+(width-letter.width)//2,y+29+(104-letter.height)//2))
        draw.rectangle((x,y,x+width-1,y+height-1),outline='#d4d4d4')
    panel.save(work/f'masked-panel-{reader}.png')
